clue.text: Poems appeal to location with steps

parts.note: odes are lyric poems
SA is short for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Verses make a pitch for a place with a staircase.
explanation.walkthrough: The Odessa steps, made famous by the film Battleship Potemkin, are a giant outdoor stairway in the Ukrainian port.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ukrainian port city is famous for its Potemkin Stairs, a monumental flight down to the harbour.

clue.text: An aquatic animal will sound authorised

indicators.note: sound tells us to say the preceding words out loud and hear another word

parts.note: an aquatic animal is a fish, so this is a fish'll, contracted

explanation.surface: Some creature of the water is claimed to make a noise with official backing.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'a fish'll' quickly and it comes out as a four-syllable word meaning sanctioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Something authorised carries formal approval from those in charge, which is what official describes.

clue.text: Short comments on unjust smear about P (the original 15 9)

indicators.note: about means going round, so the scrambled letters surround the other piece
unjust suggests the letters are treated unfairly, put in a wrong order

parts.note: throughout this puzzle P stands for pig; the parenthesis points to 15 and 9 together, an unlikely flier, the pig that might fly

explanation.surface: Brief remarks on an unfair slur against someone known only by an initial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unjust' scrambles SMEAR into EAMRS, and 'about' puts it round the pig. 'Pigs might fly' is the proverbial unlikely thing, so 15 and 9 (an unlikely flier) point to the pig.
explanation.definitionFit: Epigrams are brief, witty sayings or comments, typically pointed or satirical.

clue.text: Cancel the cleaning process

definitions.meaning: to ... a plan is informally to call it off
a hard rub with a brush to get something clean

explanation.definitionFit: Scrub means both to call off an arrangement and to give a vigorous wash with a brush.

clue.text: It's a devil when fashion reaches America

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'
mode means fashion or current style
US is the United States

explanation.surface: Something wicked follows once a trend arrives in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: Asmodeus is a demon of Jewish legend, appearing in the Book of Tobit.
explanation.definitionFit: Asmodeus is a named demon in Jewish and Christian lore, the king of demons in some accounts.

clue.text: Highlights?

parts.note: read as high lights: tall lamps that stand on the floor of a room, not the best bits of something

explanation.definitionFit: These are floor lamps on a tall pole, so literally lights that stand high.

clue.text: Not quite a fruit and a nut mix for the primate

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls a little short, losing its last letter

parts.note: an orange is a citrus fruit

indicators.note: mix tells us to stir up the letters of the words beside it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe almost calling for citrus and nuts to feed an ape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the last letter of ORANGE; 'mix' rearranges A NUT into UTAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The orangutan is a great ape of Borneo and Sumatra, a member of the primate order.

clue.text: No time for sobbing when there's so much to listen to

indicators.note: no means the following piece is missing from the word

parts.note: sobbing means tearful, crying

explanation.surface: Someone stops crying because there is so much to hear.
explanation.walkthrough: TEARFUL loses its T for time.
explanation.definitionFit: To get an earful is to hear a lot, often a long scolding, so it is a great deal to listen to.

clue.text: Townships with such a lot of rain on the level

parts.note: so can mean such, as in 'so many'
wet weather means a lot of rain
O is the O level, the old British school exam

explanation.surface: Housing estates that suffer heavy rainfall on flat ground.
explanation.walkthrough: SO WET is 'such a lot of rain' read loosely; O stands for O level, a former British school exam taken at about 16.
explanation.definitionFit: Soweto is the large urban area south-west of Johannesburg whose name abbreviates South Western Townships.

clue.text: User of air-rifle in trouble

indicators.note: in trouble means disturbed, so the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Someone firing a pellet gun gets into difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated air-rifle splits: 'air' ends the definition and RIFLE is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A flier travels through the air, so is someone who makes use of it.

clue.text: Woody associate's purpose returns — to have little Ps

indicators.note: returns tells us to send the word back the way it came

parts.note: aim means purpose
to farrow is to give birth to piglets, P being pig throughout

explanation.surface: An associate's goal comes back, to produce small offspring.
explanation.walkthrough: The actress was the long-time partner of the film-maker Woody Allen, so 'Woody' is not timber.
explanation.definitionFit: The actress was Woody Allen's partner and frequent leading lady for years, so his associate.

clue.text: Home service direction to low-down persons applied to puzzler as well

indicators.note: applied to means the following pieces are attached after the first ones

parts.note: me is the setter of the puzzle speaking of themself
also means as well
NW is north-west, a compass direction
heels are cads, people of low character

explanation.surface: An instruction to the lowly also involving the crossword setter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home service' sounds like an old BBC radio station, but it is the delivery of hot food to people's homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Meals on wheels is a service delivering cooked food to elderly or housebound people at home.

clue.text: Transport for P among diamonds is often cut out

parts.note: a car is a means of transport

indicators.note: among means set in the middle of the other letters

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for the card suit diamonds, here taken twice for the plural
a boar is a male pig, P being pig throughout

explanation.surface: A vehicle for a pig among gems is frequently removed.
explanation.walkthrough: BOAR sits between D and D; 'is often cut out' points to cardboard cut-outs.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardboard is the stiff paper from which shapes and figures are commonly cut out.

clue.text: Note little P making P's noise

parts.note: G is a note in the musical scale
the runt is the smallest pig in a litter, P being pig throughout

explanation.surface: A small pig squeals while someone records the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A grunt is the low guttural sound a pig makes.

clue.text: Out of India matters require control

indicators.note: out of order, so the letters of the words that follow come out rearranged

explanation.surface: Indian affairs need managing from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The twelve letters of INDIA MATTERS rearrange to give the answer; 'require' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To administrate is to manage or run affairs, which is to control them.

clue.text: Grandmother's attempt at being a giver of milk

parts.note: nanny is a familiar word for a grandmother; the 's is not a letter
a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: Granny tries her hand at being a wet nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: Nanny is an informal name for a grandmother as well as a children's nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: A female goat is kept for its milk, so it is a giver of milk.

clue.text: You kill one that has no love? Wildly improbable

indicators.note: wildly means the remaining letters are thrown about
that has no means the following letters are taken away

parts.note: love is O, the zero score in tennis; both of the Os go

explanation.surface: Would you really murder someone loveless? It seems most unlikely.
explanation.walkthrough: YOU KILL ONE without its two Os gives YUKILLNE, which is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something improbable is not likely to happen, the same meaning exactly.

clue.text: Affectedly pretty and idly dressed in country style

parts.note: twee means sweet or pretty in an affected way

indicators.note: dressed means arranged, so the letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone clothed in a cute, lazy, rural look.
explanation.walkthrough: IDLY dressed gives DILY.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweedy suggests the hearty country gentry who wear tweed, so this adverb means in that rural fashion.

clue.text: Topless cloth has radiance (with new inclusion) where Browning wished to be

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: linen is a cloth

indicators.note: inclusion means letters are included inside the word

parts.note: glow is radiance
and can stand for with

explanation.surface: A bare-topped garment gives off a light, with something new included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' drops L from the cloth, giving INEN. Robert Browning wrote 'Oh, to be in England / Now that April's there'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from Browning's Home-Thoughts, from Abroad, voicing his longing for his homeland.

clue.text: P in paper used to rule in Japan

indicators.note: in means the first piece is put inside the second

parts.note: The Sun is a British newspaper
a hog is a pig, P being pig throughout

explanation.surface: A pig in the newspaper once held power in Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: A shogun was a hereditary military dictator who governed Japan until 1868, so one who used to rule.

clue.text: Practice for contest with 1,000 as target

parts.note: a war is a contest between forces
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
up can mean aimed at, as in being up for something

explanation.surface: A rehearsal before a match, aiming for a thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm-up is preparatory exercise or practice before an event.

clue.text: The mob on duty?

parts.note: a ... is a gangster's muscleman, and ... duty means hard-wearing

explanation.definitionFit: A heavy is a thug from the mob, and the word also pairs with duty to mean robust.

clue.text: P meat inclined to perish in Susan's place

parts.note: ham is meat from a pig, P being pig throughout

indicators.note: inclined means tilted out of line, so the letters are set askew

explanation.surface: Pork that is likely to go off where Susan lives.
explanation.walkthrough: PERISH rearranged gives PSHIRE. Susan Hampshire is an English actress; Hampshire is also a pig breed and a county of southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The actress Susan Hampshire carries the county's name, so it is the place in her name.

clue.text: Lie on the floor?

definitions.meaning: a storey is a floor of a building, spelt this way in American English

explanation.definitionFit: A story is a fib, and in American spelling it is also a level of a building.

clue.text: P meat belonging to the crown? They're kidding

parts.note: gammon is cured meat from a pig, P being pig throughout
ER is Elizabeth Regina, so ER's is the Queen's

explanation.surface: Bacon owned by royalty, as people pull your leg.
explanation.walkthrough: To gammon is old slang for to hoax or kid.
explanation.definitionFit: To gammon is to deceive or humbug, so those doing it are kidding.

clue.text: Daggers drawn from those going to be listed

indicators.note: drawn from means the letters are extracted from the words that follow

explanation.surface: Weapons pulled out against those about to be named.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run through 'to be listed'. Obeli are dagger symbols used in printing.
explanation.definitionFit: An obelus is the dagger sign used in printing for footnotes, so obeli are daggers.

clue.text: Looking after one's own people the wrong way when drug is inhaled

annotationWithheld.why: Looking after one's own people the wrong way when drug is inhaled (8): POT inside NE..ISM is clear, but no reading of 'the wrong way' gives NEISM without a word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Looking after one's own people the wrong way when drug is inhaled

clue.text: Opposition maybe producing wise report in every other letter

definitions.text: Opposition maybe producing wise report in every other letter

parts.words: Opposition maybe producing wise report in every other letter
parts.note: opposition is an astronomical alignment; 'wise' heard is the plural of the letter Y, found in alternate places of the word

explanation.definitionFit: Syzygy is the alignment of three celestial bodies, of which opposition and conjunction are examples.
